To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(i) The performance of the heat transfer equipment is a strong function of the thermophysical properties of the working fluid.

the new simulation approach, which includes the effects of transport properties and optimized heat exchangers, provides better predictions than the thermodynamic property-only approach for the same refrigerants and operating conditions.

(a) the use of thermodynamic properties alone in preliminary refrigerant screening is not sufficient to identify the best refrigerants for a given application and (b) the use of the new model, which includes the effect of thermophysical properties in the heat exchanger and optimizes the refrigerant mass flow in the heat exchange, leads to better refrigerant selections.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the evaluation of the refrigerants for use in automotive air conditioning.
the development and validation of a new refrigerant screening model for use in evaluating the thermodynamic and transport properties of new refrigerants.
developing an improved simulation methodology to assess refrigerant performance, and to provide guidance for selecting a refrigerant for an application.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the new model is able to predict the system performance with a higher accuracy than the conventional model, and the difference in the predicted COP is significant.
the model based on thermophysical properties alone over-predicts COP by 2-3% and that the model based solely on thermodynamic properties under-predicts COP for the same system by 2-4%.
the new model is more accurate than the traditional model and is capable of predicting the performance of a refrigeration system with greater precision than the traditional model.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the new model provides more accurate and realistic predictions than a model based on properties alone and that the new model can be used for screening refrigerants and optimizing heat exchanger performance.
the thermodynamic model alone under-predicts the Coefficient of Perfor-mance of refrigerant mixtures by up to 10%.
the new model provides more accurate predictions of system performance, particularly when refrigerants with high heat transfer and pressure drops are used.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the performance of refrigerants in a given system can vary significantly when thermodynamic and transport properties are accounted for, and the impact of these properties is particularly strong for refrigerants with high molecular weight and high viscosity.
the thermodynamic properties and heat exchanger performance must be considered together in order to accurately predict system performance.

the use of thermophysical properties in the simulation model is important for refrigerant selection and performance evaluation, and that the use of a model that includes refrigerant mass flux optimization in the heat exchanger design is important for the selection of the refrigerant and the design of the heat exchanger.
